trial_name.text: Study 14595 - Pivotal 'Histopathology' Study (also referenced as Study A in labeling)

citations.quote: ## 5.3.1 Study 14595 – Pivotal ‘Histopathology’ Study

All subjects in the “Histopathology Read Study” are from the Phase 3 Study 14595 (pivotal ‘Histopathology’ study), which finished subject enrollment, but continued to follow enrolled subjects to obtain post-mortem histopathology results on deceased subjects.

design.text: Open-label, non-randomized study comparing florbetaben F18 PET imaging to postmortem histopathology (standard of truth based on Bielschowsky Silver Staining per CERAD criteria with immunohistochemistry) in terminally ill subjects who consented to post-mortem brain examination.

citations.quote: One pivotal Phase 3 studyStudy 14595: *"An open-label, non-randomized study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of BAY 94-9172 (ZK 6013443) positron emission t

In the applicant's efficacy analyses, primary efficacy endpoints are sensitivity and specificity of visual assessment F-18 florbetaben PET, compared to histopathology SOT of neuritic plaques as assessed by Bielschowsky Silver Staining in combination with immunohistochemistry [BSS(CERAD)/IHC].

population.text: Safety population of 216 subjects including 137 with Alzheimer's Disease, 31 with other dementia, 5 with Dementia with Lewy Body, 32 non-demented volunteers, and 11 young healthy volunteers; images from 82 autopsied subjects were interpreted against the subject-level histopathology standard of truth.

citations.quote: The safety population of the study is comprised of 216 subjects, including 137 subjects with Alzheimer’s Disease (AD), 31 subjects with other dementia, 5 subjects with Dementia with Lewy Body (DLB), 32 age-matched controls (“NDV”, i.e. non-demented volunteers), and 11 young healthy volunteers.
Interpretation of images from 82 autopsied subjects was compared to the subject level histopathology SoT.

endpoint.text: Co-primary endpoints of sensitivity and specificity of visual assessment of florbetaben F18 PET compared to histopathology standard of truth; prespecified sensitivity threshold 0.6 and specificity threshold 0.5, with the lower 95% CI limit required to exceed these thresholds for at least 3 of 5 blinded readers.

citations.quote: Sensitivity and specificity of visual assessment of F-18 Florbetaben PET images are co-primary endpoints of the study. Prespecified sensitivity threshold is 0.6, and specificity threshold is 0.5. Three out of 5 blinded readers must win on both sensitivity and specificity for the study to be considered a win.

n.text: Images from 205 subjects evaluated; 82 autopsied subjects interpreted against subject-level histopathology standard of truth.

citations.quote: Study A evaluated Neuraceq PET images from 205 subjects and compared the results to postmortem truth standard assessments of brain \beta-amyloid neuritic plaque density in subjects who died during the study.
Interpretation of images from 82 autopsied subjects was compared to the subject level histopathology SoT.

result.text: Study met co-primary endpoints: 3 of 5 readers achieved prespecified sensitivity and specificity thresholds, so the combined null hypotheses were rejected. In labeling (in-person training readers), median sensitivity was 98% (range 96-98) and median specificity 80% (range 77-83).

citations.quote: Overall 3 out of 5 readers achieved prespecified sensitivity and specificity thresholds, and the combined null hypotheses can be rejected.

indication.text: Radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for Positron Emission Tomography (PET) imaging of the brain to estimate β-amyloid neuritic plaque density in adult patients with cognitive impairment who are being evaluated for Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and other causes of cognitive decline.

citations.quote: Neuraceq is indicated for Positron Emission Tomography (PET) imaging of the brain to estimate \beta-amyloid neuritic plaque density in adult patients with cognitive impairment who are being evaluated for Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and other causes of cognitive decline.

target_moa.text: Florbetaben F18 is an F18-labeled stilbene derivative that binds to β-amyloid plaques in the brain; after IV administration it crosses the blood brain barrier and shows differential retention in brain regions containing β-amyloid deposits, and the F18 isotope produces a positron signal detected by a PET scanner.

citations.quote: Florbetaben F18 is a F18-labeled stilbene derivative, which binds to \beta-amyloid plaques in the brain. The F 18 isotope produces a positron signal that is detected by a PET scanner.
Following intravenous administration, Neuraceq crosses the blood brain barrier and shows differential retention in brain regions that contain \beta-amyloid deposits.

modality.text: Radiopharmaceutical (F18-labeled stilbene derivative small-molecule PET imaging agent).

citations.quote: Florbetaben is a radiopharmaceutical diagnostic agent proposed for use with positron emission tomography for detection of beta amyloid in the brain in patients evaluated for Alzheimer's disease or other causes of cognitive decline.

key_safety.text: No serious adverse reactions related to Neuraceq administration were reported. The most commonly reported adverse reactions were injection site reactions: pain (3.9%), erythema (1.7%), and irritation (1.2%). Safety is based on 978 administrations to 872 subjects.

citations.quote: The most commonly reported adverse reactions were: injection site reaction consisting of erythema (1.7 %), irritation (1.2 %), and pain (3.9 %) (6).

The overall safety profile of Neuraceq is based on data from 978 administrations of Neuraceq to 872 subjects and 12 subjects who received vehicle only. No serious adverse reactions related to Neuraceq administration have been reported.

detail.text: A REMS is not necessary; the main safety concern is radiation risk and the Division agreed a REMS is not needed to manage the risk.

citations.quote: I agree with Dr. Vega's assessment (OSE/DRISK) that the main safety concern associated to the use of florbetaben is the risk of radiation and that a REMS is not necessary to manage the risk.

vote.text: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues that would benefit from discussion.

citations.quote: Your application for Neuraceq (florbetaben F18 injection) was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from an advisory committee discussion.

detail.text: Although a complete response action was anticipated because the initial efficacy data were inadequate, the applicant submitted a new clinical study as a major amendment that provided the confirmatory evidence of efficacy, the PDUFA goal date was extended, and the application was approved in the same review cycle; no actual Complete Response Letter was issued.

citations.quote: A complete response action for the application was anticipated because the efficacy data in the initial NDA submission were not adequate to establish the effectiveness of florbetaben F 18 as an amyloid imaging agent.
For these reasons the Division designated the submission as a major amendment and extended the PDUFA review goal date.

Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated December 21, 2012, received December 21, 2012, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Neuraceq (florbetaben F18 injection), 50 to 5000 MBq/mL (1.4 to 135 mCi/mL).

basis.text: A complete response action was anticipated due to inadequate efficacy data in the initial NDA submission, but instead the applicant submitted a major amendment with new confirmatory data and the application was approved without an actual CRL being issued.

citations.quote: A complete response action for the application was anticipated because the efficacy data in the initial NDA submission were not adequate to establish the effectiveness of florbetaben F 18 as an amyloid imaging agent.

summary.text: Neuraceq (florbetaben F18) was a 505(b)(1) new molecular entity NDA given standard review. Approval was based on a pivotal Phase 3 histopathology study (14595) comparing PET visual assessment to postmortem histopathology; after a complete response was anticipated, the applicant submitted new confirmatory reader data as a major amendment, the PDUFA date was extended, and the NDA was approved without a REMS or postmarketing requirements.

citations.quote: On December 21, 2012 Piramal Imaging SA submitted an original 505(b)(1) New Drug Application (NDA 204677) for Neuraceq (florbetaben F 18 injection).

Application Type NDA (NME)
Application Number(s) 204677
Priority or Standard Standard
For these reasons the Division designated the submission as a major amendment and extended the PDUFA review goal date.
No Postmarketing Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies or other Postmarketing Requirements and Commitments are needed.

description.text: Removed limitations of use and added indication for selection of patients indicated for amyloid beta-directed therapy; added quantitative image analysis

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for changes to the INDICATIONS AND USAGE section of the prescribing information by removing the limitations of use and adding a new indication, specifically, use for selection of patients who are indicated for amyloid beta-directed therapy as described in the prescribing information of the therapeutic products. In addition, the use of quantitative image analysis is added to the Image Display and Interpretation subsection of the DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION section.
